notes:
First attempt succeeded, no retries needed. Body sent flat ({"name": ...}) since describeCapability declared no wrapper/json_path for this capability's single body field -- the JSON_PATH WRAPPER TRAP did not apply here, nothing to try both ways on. Response came back under 'configuration' (not 'data'), matching the declared 200 schema; the only undeclared field was 'is_valid_on_bstack:false' on the created record, which the schema's properties list omits (a smaller, milder version of the same gap already flagged on get_configurations_v1's item shape -- both the create and list schemas in this index under-declare fields the backing service actually returns). No declared field was missing.

SCOPE FINDING (the specific interest of this probe): the created configuration landed at GROUP level, not project level, confirming the capability's own guidance text ('Group-scoped, not project-scoped: project_id matches the route but is never sent onward'). Verified two ways: (1) group_id on the created record is 3452, the same group_id every row in the existing 244-configuration pool carries; (2) a follow-up get_configurations_v1 call against the SAME project_id (379335744) with per_page=300 (no name filter) returned info.count=245 and 245 rows -- i.e. the pool visible from PR-2005's own route grew from the pre-write baseline of 244 to 245, and the new row (id 5189868, name '__mcp-probe-config-20260921') is present in that undifferentiated list alongside the pre-existing configurations. A separate name-filtered read (q=__mcp-probe-config-20260921) also returned exactly one row, same id, confirming the write round-trips cleanly. Conclusion: this is a genuinely group-wide, blast-radius write -- calling create_configuration_v1 through ANY project in group 3452 adds to the same shared pool every other project in that group reads from. There is no project-scoped variant; an agent that assumes project_id constrains the write is wrong, and duplicate-by-name creation is not prevented (per guidance) so repeated/retried calls would silently multiply entries in the shared pool.

TR-9062 / TC-54457 configuration-null contradiction: NOT chased in this probe. create_configuration_v1's response (a plain new configuration record with no run/mapping linkage) and the get_configurations_v1 follow-up read (a flat list of configuration rows, no run or case-mapping fields) neither one surfaces any case-configuration mapping data, so this probe's own response shape sheds no light on which configuration(s) TC-54457's two TR-9062 mapping_ids actually point at. That contradiction needs a dedicated probe against the test-run/case-mapping read capabilities (e.g. get_test_cases_for_v1_test_run), not this one.
